title: RWB-S9-E7013-APP: the partner review has no rule row, no operation, no action list, no column, no event and no in-service build row for its scorecard
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E7013-APP; context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 2, 4, 5, 8 and 12, Temporal and Drools slides 1 to 3); legacy RWB-E7-013; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A1.3, A1.4, A2.8, A2.10 and Requirements served; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.1 to T5.3, T6.1, T7 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40 and R-UNI-45; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-PRM-10; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 API-S9-001 to API-S9-006
description: (1) No rule row of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 names a partner review and there is no partner route set at all: the partner rows are R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29 and R-UNI-45, and every one of them is a recall, a re-selection or a conduct report that follows a review, so the review's own rule ID and route set have no source. (2) None of the six REST operations of the service records a review: GET /partners, POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, GET /partner/instructions, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results and POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices serve the panel, an instruction, an acceptance, a result and an invoice, with first-in epics Epic 2 to Epic 6, and the review read behind SCR-34 and SCR-35 is unpublished. (3) The statuses the reviewer records and the actions taken per point have no published list: no LOV-REVIEW-STATUS or LOV-REVIEW-ACTION exists in TSD S9 T3.2 or the reference-data document, and the action list is therefore a placeholder. (4) No column of partner or partner_instruction carries the review, a point or an action: TSD S9 T3.1 gives seven partner fields and nine instruction fields, so the review lives on its decision record and the key raises no table, no column and no migration. (5) A review publishes no event: the service owns EV-20 InstructionIssued and EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted, and both report an instruction or a result. (6) The legacy story depends on FEAT-PRM-08 Score partners monthly, whose output is partner.score; the plan carries no H row to RWB-S9-E7011-APP and no C row, so the dependency is served by a seeded field inside the same service and is not a build dependency. (7) The plan gives C, I and X empty while the act consumes the rule package of rwb-decision (P7) and the reference data and lists of rwb-case (P3), and DP-04, DP-06 and DP-07 are not in the key's pattern set. (8) FSD S9 A2.10.3.3 names the Head of Litigation and the Head of Asset Liquidity as also using the review while TSD S9 T6.1 gives both RA, so the act right U and the approver right A do not sit on the same role. (9) The legacy Data table names partner, decision_log_entry and rule_row, two of which are other owners' tables, and the legacy Depends on FEAT-PRM-08 has no plan row. (10) TSD S9 T4 gives the module no state machine and no job, so the act has no workflow and no Schedule of its own.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.10.1 to A2.10.4.4 (objective, one metric, three flow steps, integration point Partner portal, prerequisite FEAT-PRM-08, VR-S9-010-1, BR-S9-010, the eight field-catalog rows, Partner and agency manager primary with the Head of Litigation and the Head of Asset Liquidity also using, AC-S9-010-01, the two exception criteria and no background event); FSD S9 Requirements served REQ-S9-001 (the six points), REQ-S9-002, REQ-S9-007 and REQ-S9-008; TSD S9 T2 (write the decision log entry before any change), T3.0 (standard record columns), T3.1 (the seven partner and nine instruction fields, DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016), T3.2 (LOV-INSTR-STATUS, LOV-INSTRUCTION, LOV-PANEL, LOV-PARTNER-TYPE), T3.3 (the two relationships to recovery_case and partner), T4 (no state machine, acts on P3 events), T5.1 (INT-24 Partner portal both directions), T5.2 (published interfaces of P3, P4, P5, P6 and P7), T5.3 (InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted published), T6.1 (RW-AGENCYMG CRUDA, RW-HEADLIT and RW-HEADASL RA) and T-A.1 (the six operations, first in Epic 2 to Epic 6); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40 and R-UNI-45; context pack S9 ownership rows (three tables, six operations, two events, no job, one workflow) and service row (wave 4); Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-PRM-10 (Partner and agency manager, Partner portal, FEAT-PRM-08); legacy RWB-E7-013 Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Endpoints, Screen and states, Permission checks and Validation and messages.
area: Business rules, data model, API contract, access, reference data, events
owner_role: Center of excellence with the solution architect, the rwb-decision rule owner, the rwb-access owner and the rwb-case reference-data owner
proposed: Publish one partner route set with a review row, its event and its route to the partner and agency manager; publish the review act and its read, or accept that the review is a composite-route read with the entry written behind it; publish the status list, the action list and the six-point list with their versions; decide whether a review is stored on partner (a new field or a review table) or on the decision record only; decide whether a review publishes an event of its own; add the in-service H row to RWB-S9-E7011-APP for the scorecard; settle the act and the read rights for the two heads of function. Until then the review evaluates the package in force, records on its entry, writes no column, publishes nothing and carries the placeholders.

title: RWB-S9-E7013-CON: the consumed operation names, the review read, the entry attributes, the action list and the review column have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E7013-CON; context pack S9 rwb-partner; legacy RWB-E7-013; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A2.10.3.1, A2.10.3.2, A2.10.3.3, A2.10.4 and Screens; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40 and R-UNI-45; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 API-S9-001 to API-S9-006; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-PRM-10
description: (1) No source publishes an operation that reads the rule package for a review or the reference data of the six points, so both consumed rows carry a placeholder and their owners are fixed only by TSD S9 T5.2 and the R3 default ruling. (2) The review read behind SCR-34 and SCR-35 is unpublished, and the six operations of the service all belong to earlier stories with first-in epics Epic 2 to Epic 6, so the baseline declares no operation and cannot give the act a seventh. (3) The review-entry attributes have no schema of their own: the local record of DP-03 is a library object and no source fixes the names, the point values, the action values or the reviewer attribute, so the baseline proposes them and the library owner confirms. (4) The statuses and the actions per point have no published list, so the entry cannot declare a closed enumeration and the values are reference data with a placeholder. (5) No column of partner or partner_instruction carries the review, so both elements are declared unchanged and the review lives on its entry. (6) TSD S9 T3.1 describes only two of the three tables the Ownership Map gives the service: partner_user is named by the context pack and is not described in the TSD, so the baseline declares it as owned without an element. (7) A review publishes no event: EV-20 and EV-21 are InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted of the instruction stories. (8) The plan's C row is empty although the act consumes rwb-decision and rwb-case, and DP-04, DP-06 and DP-07 are not in the pattern set although the package and the reference data are consumed. (9) FSD S9 A2.10.3.3 names the two heads of function as also using the review while TSD S9 T6.1 gives both RA, so the baseline records the right rather than widening it. (10) EP07 is wave 4 and rwb-partner is wave 4, so the waves agree and only the date needs the tentative mark.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.10.2 to A2.10.4.4 (the three steps, the integration point, the prerequisite, VR-S9-010-1, BR-S9-010, the eight field-catalog rows, the two roles and the two heads of function, AC-S9-010-01, the two exception criteria, no background event); FSD S9 Screens (SCR-34 Partner list, SCR-35 Placement and allocation, SCR-36 Partner scorecard, PRT-01 to PRT-04); TSD S9 T2 (record the decision before the change), T3.0 (standard record columns), T3.1 (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016), T3.2 (the four lists), T3.3 (the two relationships), T4 (no state machine; acts on P3 events), T5.2 (the published interfaces of P3 to P7), T5.3 (InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted), T6.1 (RW-AGENCYMG CRUDA, the U holders, RW-HEADLIT and RW-HEADASL RA, the partner portal users RU) and T-A.1 (the six operations and their rights); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40 and R-UNI-45; context pack S9 ownership rows (three tables, six operations, two events, no job, one workflow) and service row (wave 4); legacy RWB-E7-013 Endpoints, Screen and states, Permission checks and Validation and messages.
area: API contract, data model, access, reference data, events
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-decision owner, the rwb-case reference-data owner, the rwb-access owner and the platform library owner
proposed: Publish the rule-package read and the reference-data read with their fields and their 2 s budget; publish the review read or confirm that it is a composite-route read with no operation; confirm the review-entry attributes against the local record schema; publish the status list and the action list with their versions; describe partner_user in the TSD; confirm that no review event is published in wave 4; record the two heads of function as readers and approvers. Until then the baseline declares the two consumed rows with the placeholders, the two unchanged elements and the three absences.
